narration_timeline.text: A swan can look peaceful one moment and be airborne the next. What happens between those flights?
narration_timeline.scene: Swans visibly flying above a misty lake, not gliding on the water.

narration_timeline.text: On misty mornings, swans gather on the grass beside the water, stretching their long necks.
narration_timeline.scene: Two or more white swans standing together on grass in morning mist.

narration_timeline.text: At the pond, one bird splashes its feathers while a nearby nest waits among the reeds.
narration_timeline.scene: Swan splashing its feathers in pond followed by visible swan nest in reeds.

narration_timeline.text: Others rest on green banks, or move slowly past lily-covered corners of the park.
narration_timeline.scene: Swans resting on a grassy bank, followed by swans near lily-covered pond and park building.

narration_timeline.text: The distant pond looks empty until two white swans appear near its edge.
narration_timeline.scene: Wide landscape of pond, with two white swans only appearing toward the end of the clip.

narration_timeline.text: And when the flock takes off, broad wings carry them over the water in a completely different kind of glide.
narration_timeline.scene: Several swans flying above water in a flock.
